questions.question: Nadia's class builds a rectangular vegetable bed at school. It is 8 m long and 6 m wide. What is the area of the bed?
questions.explain: Area of a rectangle = length × width, so 8 × 6 = 48 m². The usual trap is adding the sides (8+6=14) or finding the distance around the bed (28 m) — that is perimeter, not area.

questions.question: Jasper is sorting 3-D objects by their faces. Which statement correctly describes a triangular prism?
options: It has 1 triangular base and 3 triangular faces that meet at a point.
It has 2 triangular faces and 4 rectangular faces, 6 faces in all.
It has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces, 5 faces in all.
All of its faces are triangles.
questions.explain: A prism has two identical bases joined by rectangles, so a triangular prism has 2 triangles + 3 rectangles = 5 faces. Many students pick the shape whose faces meet at a point — that is a pyramid, not a prism.

questions.question: In a woven cedar basket design, one leaf shape appears again 4 squares to the right. The copy is the same size and faces exactly the same way. Which single transformation moved the shape?
options: A flip and then a turn
questions.explain: A slide moves a shape a set distance without changing its size or the way it faces, so the design shows a translation. If the copy had faced the opposite way it would be a flip — check the direction the shape points before choosing.

questions.question: Leo's hockey practice at the community rink starts at 4:45 p.m. and ends at 6:20 p.m. How long is the practice?
questions.explain: Count up: 4:45 → 5:45 is 1 hour, then 5:45 → 6:20 is 35 more minutes, so 1 h 35 min. The trap is subtracting like decimal numbers (6.20 − 4.45), because an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.question: Mateo is stapling ribbon all the way around the edge of a rectangular bulletin board that is 90 cm long and 60 cm wide. How much ribbon does he need?
questions.explain: Going around the edge means perimeter: 90 + 60 + 90 + 60 = 300 cm. The common mistake is multiplying (90 × 60 = 5400), which gives the area of the board's surface, or adding just one length and one width (150 cm).

questions.question: A rectangular patio behind Emma's house measures 400 cm along one side and 3 m along the other. What is the area of the patio in square metres?
questions.explain: Convert first: 400 cm = 4 m, then 4 × 3 = 12 m². The biggest trap is multiplying 400 × 3 before converting — both measurements must be in the same unit.

questions.question: Two rectangular garden plots at the community garden each need 24 m of fencing to go all the way around. Plot A is 8 m by 4 m, and Plot B is 9 m by 3 m. Which statement is true?
options: The plots have the same area, because they have the same perimeter.
Plot B has the larger area, by 5 m².
Plot A has the larger area, by 5 m².
The areas cannot be compared without more measurements.
questions.explain: Both perimeters are 24 m, but the areas are 8 × 4 = 32 m² and 9 × 3 = 27 m², so Plot A is larger by 5 m². The most common misconception in this unit is thinking equal perimeter forces equal area — the closer a rectangle is to a square, the more area it holds.

questions.question: Amara's family is catching the 2:15 p.m. ferry. The drive from home to the terminal takes 1 h 50 min, and they must be lined up at the terminal 30 minutes before the sailing time. What is the latest time they can leave home?
questions.explain: Work backwards in two steps: 2:15 − 30 min = 1:45 p.m. to be in line, then 1:45 − 1 h = 12:45, − 50 min = 11:55 a.m. The traps are forgetting the 30-minute line-up time (12:25 p.m.) and taking away only 40 minutes instead of regrouping an hour into 60 minutes.
